title: Python: common control and data schedule engine
description:
Extend python/src/lichen/sim/tdma.py and python/src/lichen/timing/tdma_fsm.py to produce receiver-aware control/data opportunities from the finalized schedule contract. Single-radio participants return for common CH0 windows except during eligible control TX. Include activation, expiry, settling, clock uncertainty and finite radio resources. Profile 0x01 remains SF10/BW125k/CR4/5 with the specified preamble, header, CRC and LDRO settings throughout its generation.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Compose python.04 grants, python.06 operation costs and python.12 synchronization. Do not invent a universal cadence, adaptive controller, mandatory hopping or multi-radio requirement. Existing slot-candidate and timing helpers are reusable but not evidence of receiver availability. Hardware is represented by explicit finite capabilities; this offline work grants no RF permission and preserves baseline SCHC/security and radio identity ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Run vectors.04/.06 through the production scheduler with an independently specified one-radio event trace. Verify no simultaneous channels or RX/TX obligations, common-window return, control exchanges fitting geometry, expired schedules, overlapping DODAG interference assumptions and no density/load-triggered channel or SF changes. Test actual start/end opportunities rather than a duplicate algorithm in validate_vector. Extend python/tests/sim/test_tdma.py and python/tests/timing/test_tdma_fsm.py; run scoped pytest and ruff.
